title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — per hominem mors/resurrectio: one in kind, many in number—not imputed singular death
pass_a_gloss: On the prior verse (death and resurrection come by a man): not Adam's one death or Christ's one rising imputed to the rest, but death and rising one in kind and many in number, each his own. Placeus treats that as plain without further proof.
pass_b_english: And when in the preceding verse the Apostle speaks thus—since by a man comes death, by a man also comes the resurrection of the dead—he does not mean one Adam's death imputed to the rest of men, nor one Christ's resurrection imputed, but death and resurrection one in kind, many in number, by which all die and rise, each his own. That is so plain it needs no proof.
source_text: Et cum versu praecedente Apostolus sic loquitur: quandoquidem per hominem est mors, etiam per hominem est resurrectio mortuorum, non intelligit unius Adami mortem reliquis hominibus imputatam nec unius Christi resurrectionem imputatam, sed mortem & resurrectionem specie unam, numero multam, qua omnes, quisque sua, moriuntur & resurgunt. Id ita manifestum est ut probatione non egeat.
